newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Swiss franc deals dominate slow Hungary FX futures.
newsitem.headline: Swiss franc deals dominate slow Hungary FX futures.

text.p: Hungary's foreign currency futures markets saw modest turnover dominated by deals in the Swiss franc and mark, dealers said.
Total turnover of foreign currency futures on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) was 2.84 billion forints, down from Tuesday's 4.33 billion.
"A good part of these deals were due to one bank selling francs and buying marks," said Mihaly Otvos of OTP Forex.
December Swiss franc accounted for 7,775 contracts out of a total 20,986 contracts turnover, while 5,700 contracts for December marks changed hands.
The Swiss franc went down 0.70 forints for September to 132.80 and finished at 138.00 for December, down 0.45.
"Spot prices were the main reason for the drop in franc futures...and some players expect the fall to continue," Otvos said.
German mark futures were mixed as September closed at 112.45, down 0.05 and at 116.41 for December, up 0.11.
The central bank quoted the two currencies in its midday fix at 123.36 forints to the Swiss franc, down 0.37, and the mark at 105.31 forints, up 0.07.

The much smaller currency futures section of the Budapest Stock Exchange saw one deal for December dollars with the price rising 0.07 forints to 196.00 and two deals for December marks wich eased to 116.80, down 0.80.
